status: PROPOSED - a mapping table, not a conformance claim
aas1_source: https://aas-1.org/ (v0.1, May 2026, CC0; 5 record classes, 12 assertions, RFC 8785 JCS, SHA-256, AIS-1 binding)
what_this_is: It maps what this implementation actually checks onto AAS-1 assertion names, and states where it has nothing. It does not claim AAS-1 conformance; AAS-1 has no conformance suite yet (its 2027 roadmap lists one).

record_classes_touched.A: uibc evidence package (one submission with its evidence index and seal) is closest to a Class A record, but AAS-1's Class A is an agent action, not a package verdict - so this is a shape similarity, not equivalence
record_classes_touched.D: the uibc verify report has the shape of a Class D finding (per-check results + overall verdict), but it is issued by the implementation, not by an auditor: no materiality basis, no engagement reference

assertions.name: Existence
assertions.honest_note: proves the package is well formed and internally consistent; does not prove the recorded action took place

assertions.name: Completeness
assertions.honest_note: checks the index against what is present in the package, not against what should have been recorded

assertions.name: Accuracy
assertions.honest_note: accuracy of hashes, not accuracy of the underlying claim about the world

assertions.name: Authorisation
assertions.honest_note: proves the seal verifies against the key recorded in the package; delegation scope is outside the boundary

assertions.name: Cutoff
assertions.honest_note: format strictness only; external timestamp anchoring is in not_checked

assertions.name: Presentation
assertions.honest_note: presentation here means byte-canonical form, not fair presentation of findings

assertions.name: Identity
assertions.honest_note: identity consistency inside the package; anchoring requires a pinned key or DID, and the HTTP transport cannot express it

assertions.name: Provenance
assertions.honest_note: model, tools, prompt context and data sources are not captured anywhere in this implementation

assertions.name: Reproducibility
assertions.honest_note: the same input reproduces the same report byte for byte; the underlying evaluation is not re-derivable by a third party from the record alone

assertions.name: Independence
assertions.honest_note: agent action vs operator override is not separable in this implementation; see also the corpus-ownership note: the 288-vector corpus is third-party, but the rail is ours

summary.reading: half of AAS-1's assertions are touched at package level, four are entirely absent, none is fully satisfied. The absent four (Classification, Provenance, Policy Compliance, Independence) are exactly what an action-record format would supply, which is why attaching to AAS-1 instead of inventing a parallel vocabulary is the cheaper path.

next_actions.action: Read AAS-1 v0.1 specification + Audit Manual before any mapping is published
Decide: emit Class A records (new capability) or stay a verification rail and publish this table as a gap analysis
If staying a rail: offer the 288-vector run as evidence material to AAS-1's planned conformance suite (2027)
